wording: R0, the expected number of secondary cases one case produces in a completely susceptible population, is usually read as a threshold (an outbreak continues if R0 > 1 and ends if R0 < 1), but it is not a biological constant, not a rate (it says nothing about how fast cases appear), not a measure of severity, and vaccination lowers the effective reproduction number R, not R0; reported values vary widely (measles 3.7-203.3 in one review) and some are obsolete.
confidence: High as a report of the review
counterevidence_limits: Perspective article; the figures are P26's citations.
operationalization: APP Insurgence = emergence of an outbreak when cases more than replace themselves
verification_phrases: P26|an outbreak is expected to continue if R 0 has a value >1 and to end if R 0 is <1 || P26|R 0 is most accurately described in terms of cases per case || P26|this activity will technically not reduce the R 0 value || P26|R 0 is not a biological constant for a pathogen

wording: In a branching model of one introduced case, no outbreak reached 1,000 cases at R0 = 0.8; at R0 = 1.5 and 3 major outbreaks occurred in 58.1% and 94.1% of 20,000 runs (theory 58.3%, 94.0%), so even above the threshold many introductions die out. Changing the generation time from 3 to 15 days left the outbreak probability unchanged and stretched the time to 1,000 cases five-fold (44 vs 219 days at R0 = 1.5), illustrating P26's point that R0 is not a rate.
counterevidence_limits: Homogeneous Poisson offspring; fully susceptible population.
operationalization: APP Insurgence = outbreak emergence above R0 = 1

wording: P26 notes that removing susceptible people by vaccination does not technically reduce R0, because R0 assumes a completely susceptible population; for vaccination the appropriate metric is the effective reproduction number R, which does not assume complete susceptibility.
locator: P26 section on R0 and vaccination (read in full in IN0)
counterevidence_limits: Definitional point; P26 gives no formula for R.
operationalization: APP Insurgence = outbreak potential in a partly immune population
verification_phrases: P26|the more appropriate metric to use is the effective reproduction number

wording: Near the threshold the share of introductions reaching 1,000 cases was 9.36% at R0 = 1.05 (theory 9.37%) and 31.6% at 1.2 (31.4%); 'no major outbreak below 1' was not supported: at R0 = 0.95, 0.16% of chains (32 of 20,000) still reached 1,000 cases, after 64 generations on average. Just below the threshold, rare large chains occur.
counterevidence_limits: 'Major' means reaching K = 1000; V1 passed at R0 = 0.95 only through the pre-set 0.002 allowance (disclosed).
operationalization: APP Insurgence = outbreak emergence near R0 = 1

wording: With superspreading (negative-binomial offspring, k = 0.1) the major-outbreak share fell to 7.0% at R0 = 1.5 (theory 6.8%; Poisson 58%) and 16.5% at R0 = 3 (16.2%; Poisson 94%): heterogeneity makes most introductions fail even at high R0, but those that take off are explosive. 'No major outbreak at R0 = 0.8' was not supported: one chain in 20,000 reached 1,000 cases.
counterevidence_limits: k = 0.1 illustrative; standard extinction equation, not from P26.
operationalization: APP Insurgence = emergence with heterogeneous transmission

wording: With 60% random immunity, R0 = 2 gave R = 0.8 and no chain reached 1,000 cases in 20,000; R0 = 3 and 4 gave R = 1.2 and 1.6 and major-outbreak shares 30.9% and 64.4%, matching 1 - q at the reduced R (31.4%, 64.2%): what decides emergence is the effective number R (P26), not R0.
operationalization: APP Insurgence = emergence suppressed by immunity

wording: P32's review of SARS-CoV-2 transmission found that 67% of index cases infected no one and 3% (287) infected more than five; a negative binomial fit gave mean 0.88 and dispersion k = 0.27, implying that the top 17% of index cases generate 80% of secondary cases; k was within the 0.1-0.7 range of earlier estimates.
locator: P32 abstract, Results 'Heterogeneity in transmission across individual index cases', Table 4 (read in full)
confidence: High (systematic review, 9,883 index cases from 491 papers; pre-variant, pre-vaccination)
counterevidence_limits: Data mostly 2020, China and India; incomplete contact tracing; the offspring analysis uses 9,591 of 9,883 index cases.
operationalization: APP Insurgence = emergence driven by a few superspreaders
verification_phrases: P32|Among index cases, 67% reported zero secondary cases and only 3% (287) infected >5 secondary cases || P32|a mean of 0.88 (CI: 0.84–0.92) and a dispersion parameter k of 0.27 || P32|the top 17% most infectious index cases would be expected to generate 80% of all secondary cases

wording: P32's overall fit is internally consistent: NB(0.88, 0.27) gives 67.6% zero, 3.6% above five and 16.5% producing 80% (P32: 67%, 3%, 17%). For the symptomatic subgroup the fit NB(2.06, 0.43) is not supported against P32's reported shares (47% zero vs 44%, 11.6% above five vs 9%); the top-80% check there used a placeholder (no P32 value).
counterevidence_limits: Checks P32's summary numbers against its own fit, not the raw data.

wording: With P32's dispersion k = 0.27, the major-outbreak share was 15.1% at R0 = 1.5 and 29.9% at 2.5 (theory 15.3%, 30.2%; Poisson about 58% and 89%); at P32's own mean 0.88, 'no major outbreak' was not supported (7 of 20,000 chains reached 1,000 cases). With 50% immunity, R0 = 1.6 gave none, 2.5 gave 9.0% and 4.0 gave 24.2%, as theory.
counterevidence_limits: Mixing P32's k with other R0 values is the agent's; homogeneous immunity.
operationalization: APP Insurgence = emergence with observed heterogeneity

wording: INA's below-threshold result replicated at K = 1,000 (R0 = 0.95: 0.15% of chains, H1 again not supported), but with K = 10,000 no chain at R0 = 0.95 reached the threshold while R0 = 1.05 kept 9.3%: 'major outbreaks below 1' are an artefact of a small K, not emergence.
operationalization: APP Insurgence = what counts as an outbreak

wording: Analysing frequency records of the 10 August 1996 Western Interconnection blackout, P41 finds a persistent change (a jump in noise level) about 2 minutes before the official triggering line trip, then abrupt, nearly discontinuous state changes linked to discrete events (loss of the McNary units, failing damping) rather than smooth critical slowing down; P41 argues that common leading indicators work only for bifurcation-induced tipping, while noise-induced tipping can occur far from any bifurcation.
locator: P41 abstract, Results, Discussion (read in full)
counterevidence_limits: Single event; causal link to the tree fault is stated as plausible, not certain (P41); P41's synthetic Eq. 2 prints a noise ramp inconsistent with its own plateaus (agent's check, see INC-APP-12).
operationalization: APP Insurgence = a technical system tipping into cascading failure
verification_phrases: P41|A state change is indicated two minutes before the official triggering event || P41|The results disprove the simple idea of smooth changes in early warning metrics

wording: In P41's N-tipping system the switch time is broadly spread: 23% of 200 realisations had not switched by t = 2000 and the median among those that did was 1759, so 'switch during the ramp' was not supported (P41's single run switched at 1387). Before the switch the rolling standard deviation rose strongly (Kendall tau 0.89) and a simple least-squares estimator recovered the true drift slope (-1.92 vs -2) and noise level (1% error), but lag-1 autocorrelation also trended upward (tau 0.32), so 'no trend' was not supported narrowly.
counterevidence_limits: Switch criterion and estimator are the agent's (not P41's BLE); P41's printed ramp formula was replaced by the offset form that joins its plateaus.
operationalization: APP Insurgence = noise-induced tipping and its warning signs

wording: B-tipping comparator on P41's fold drift: with a slow ramp and weak noise the system tipped at r = -0.387 and -0.384 (fold -0.385) with a clear critical-slowing-down signal (AR1 Kendall tau 0.84); stronger noise tipped it early (-0.235), a faster ramp late (-0.431). Together with INC-APP-12: autocorrelation warns well before a fold, much less before noise-induced switching.
counterevidence_limits: Agent's comparator (P41 ramps r upward); detrending and window choices are the agent's.
operationalization: APP Insurgence = bifurcation-induced tipping and its warning

wording: Replications: P32's summary shares again consistent with its fit (67.7% zero, 3.6% > 5, 16.6%); emergence with k = 0.27 again 15.1% and 30.1% at R0 1.5 and 2.5, and at R0 0.88 10 of 20,000 again reached K = 1,000, so 'no major outbreak below 1' was again not supported at K = 1,000; at K = 10,000 none at R0 0.95 (as in INB).
